### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s).

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via SharingService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-1.mdx`  _(via SharingService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-3.mdx`  _(via SharingService (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os serve (command, 51 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **49** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1a21ce93a2f8f95a52955380ab6f296b6ab89db4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e4ad1bbcb550876ee8b38f089f02f9697c091337` — the merge of head `9c805c664c8768d9e956724018b664a3977bfeb2` into base `1a21ce93a2f8f95a52955380ab6f296b6ab89db4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e4ad1bbcb550876ee8b38f089f02f9697c091337 && git checkout e4ad1bbcb550876ee8b38f089f02f9697c091337
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1a21ce93a2f8f95a52955380ab6f296b6ab89db4 9c805c664c8768d9e956724018b664a3977bfeb2 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1a21ce93a2f8f95a52955380ab6f296b6ab89db4 && git merge --no-ff 9c805c664c8768d9e956724018b664a3977bfeb2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1a21ce93a2f8f95a52955380ab6f296b6ab89db4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1a21ce93a2f8f95a52955380ab6f296b6ab89db4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Seat check

**L1: ACCEPT on code and tests** (L1-a, for area d7-B) at head `e26a7e36bbc507b7429390b2e6efc27370a79197`, read 2026-11-20T09:03Z. One comment edit is owed before landing, as a prose-only delta (below). No L2 is owed:

- no file is under `packages/spec/src/**`, and no governed path is touched;
- the declaration is `Clause-②: no`, with no `(narrowing)` arm;
- the change adds a diagnostic and adds no error code.

### Owed before landing: the `serve.ts` comment this PR makes false

`packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts:5478` gives the start-up advisory's reason as "the sharing layer then fails closed to owner-only without a word". After this PR the runtime says it, once, at the first fallback.

This is the same falsified-silence your amendment 7033136082 fixed in `capability-preflight.ts`, and the new `ENTERPRISE_ABSENCE_RUNTIME_NOTICE` docblock states the rule ("a runtime that starts logging adds its row here in the same change, or the CLI goes on claiming a silence the server log contradicts"). The comment is the rationale the next author reads before touching either line, so leave it true when this PR lands.

The fix:

- a one-clause comment edit: the runtime logs it once at the first fallback, and `os serve` says it at start-up, before any request;
- a claim amendment naming `serve.ts`;
- a delta L1 on the new head.

The `cli` patch changeset already covers the package. No code changes and no L2 is owed.

### Code

- **Latch** (`sharing-service.ts`, `resolveOwnerScopeIds`).
  - `hierarchyResolverAbsenceNoted` is set only on the `!resolver` branch, after `own` / `org` / unset have already returned. It is set before the `warn`, inside `try`, so a throwing sink logs once and never fails the gate.
  - The resolver is still looked up on every call, and the `return [me]` is unchanged, so no answer depends on the latch.
  - One instance per boot holds: `sharing-plugin.ts` builds the service once, at `kernel:ready`.
- **Notice.**
  - The `[sharing] hierarchy scope NOT widened:` prefix is the existing no-org line's at `sharing-service.ts:2536`, so one grep finds both.
  - The provider is `PLATFORM_CAPABILITY_PROVIDERS['hierarchy-security'].package`, the registry row the CLI names.
  - `HIERARCHY_RESOLVER_ABSENT_NOTICE` is a module export only. `src/index.ts` re-exports a named list from `sharing-service.js` that does not include it, so the package entry is unchanged.
- **CLI (your point 2).** `ENTERPRISE_ABSENCE_RUNTIME_NOTICE` is fine under `Clause-②: no`.
  - `packages/cli`'s `exports` are `.`, `./console`, `./hook-body` and `./package.json`.
  - `src/index.ts` re-exports command classes, and none of `compile` / `validate` / `verify` / `serve` re-exports `capability-preflight`. `console.ts` and `hook-body.ts` export only their own utils.
  - So the table is not reachable from any entry. Keeping it separate from `ENTERPRISE_ABSENCE_CONSEQUENCE` is the right call, for the reason its docblock gives: metadata consequence versus runtime notice.
  - `enterpriseAbsenceConsequence` keeps the `hasOwnProperty` lookup for both tables.

### Tests and controls

- **Sharing:**
  - the notice names the token, the registry provider and owner-only, and opens with the prefix the CLI quotes;
  - two hierarchy calls plus a public `canManageShares` gate give one notice, with `{capability, provider, scope}`, and the owner-only answers;
  - a fresh instance says it again;
  - CONTROLS: `undefined` / `own` / `org` and an owner gate log nothing; a registered resolver widens and logs nothing;
  - a throwing logger: two calls give one `warn` and both answer `['bob']`.
- **CLI:**
  - every runtime-notice key is an `enterprise`-edition registry token;
  - `hierarchy-security` drops "no log line says so" and quotes the prefix;
  - CONTROL: an unrowed token keeps the silence clause.
- **Your point 3.** I accept the narrowed local run. CI pinned to this head carries what was skipped: `Test Core` 10/10 and `Type Check · workspace` / `source gates` / `consumer gates` / `debt ledger` / `TypeScript Type Check` are all `success`.

### Prose, sentence by sentence

- **Changeset.**
  - The three hierarchy scopes, the resolver service and the capability, provider and fail-closed are all true by the code.
  - "a runtime booted without the CLI gave an operator nothing" holds: the CLI was the only voice before.
  - "once per service instance, which is once per boot, never once per request" holds by the latch and the single construction.
  - "Nothing is logged for an app that never asks for a hierarchy scope, or when a resolver is registered" is pinned.
  - "The answer does not change" is pinned.
  - The CLI bullet matches `enterpriseAbsenceConsequence`, and "Other enterprise tokens keep their wording" is pinned by the CONTROL.
- **Bumps.** Two `patch` bumps are right.

### Gates and routing

- CI at `e26a7e36`: 39 `success`, 18 `skipped`, none red.
- After the `serve.ts` comment edit and its delta L1, `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 35780` decides the landing route.

## Seat check (delta)

**L1: ACCEPT** (L1-a, for area d7-B) at head `9c805c664c8768d9e956724018b664a3977bfeb2`, read 2026-11-20T09:12Z. This closes the one item 7035158988 owed. No L2 is owed.

- **Condition:** CI at this head finishes green. When I read, 21 runs were `success`, 18 `skipped` and 15 in progress, with none red.

### The delta

`git diff e26a7e36 9c805c66` is three comment lines in `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts`. "fails closed to owner-only without a word" becomes "fails closed to owner-only; the runtime logs that once, at the first fallback, which may be long after boot. So say it here too, once at start-up and before any request".

Each clause holds:

- `resolveOwnerScopeIds` latches on the first fallback, and the first fallback comes at the first hierarchy-scoped read, so "may be long after boot" is right;
- the start-up advisory runs in `serve` before the listener.

The edit also keeps the advisory's own reason true, since it is the earlier, request-independent voice.

- **Claim amendment 2** (7035179372) names `serve.ts`.
- **No new changeset is owed.** The existing `cli` patch covers the package.

### Gates and routing

After CI is green at `9c805c66`, `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 35780` decides the landing route.
